case.pattern_description: The fraud pattern involves five online transactions totaling $1,935.29, with each transaction just under $500, all conducted within 21 minutes on a single card. The transactions were flagged as fraudulent due to a unique pattern that did not fit any known typology. The fraud was discovered by an agent scanning the card's transaction history, identifying a series of closely spaced, small-dollar transactions that collectively exceeded the known fraud thresholds. The affected card was blocked, a case was created, and a report was filed, with the case being escalated to a human analyst for further review.

sar.narrative: Customer C03633, holder of card C03633-K1, is the subject of this report. Between 2016-11-25 21:00 and 2016-11-25 21:21, 4 transaction(s) totalling $1,935.29 were made on the card online from device profile 'MacOS | Mac OS X 10_8_5 | chrome 49.0 | 1280x800': $488.31 (3487284, 2016-11-25 21:00), $489.91 (3487318, 2016-11-25 21:10), $479.33 (3487340, 2016-11-25 21:18), $477.74 (3487348, 2016-11-25 21:21). Every amount sat just below $500 and the purchases were placed minutes apart, a pattern consistent with deliberately staying under an authorisation threshold. The activity is suspicious because: 4 online purchases within 21 minutes, each between $400 and $500 ($488.31, $489.91, $479.33, $477.74; total $1,935.29). It closely resembles earlier confirmed fraud cases CC-3748, CC-3841, CC-3907. The bank has recommended blocking and reissuing the card, placing linked cards under monitoring where applicable, and retaining the transaction, device and investigation records as supporting documentation.
